title: Union with Christ covers sins retractable by present faith-repentance—not sins not yet incurred
source_text: XXIII. Verum hic dicet aliquis, Quicunque per veram fidem & poenitentiam ad Deum se convertit, hoc ipso unitur Christo, tanquam membrum capiti, & fit unum cum Christo corpus, adeoque censetur in Christo passus & mortuus, & in eo lytrum sufficiens pro peccatis suis omnibus dependisse. Qui autem lytrum sufficiens solvit debito suo manet exsolutus: nec potest amplius esse poenae luendae reus, qua in re peccatorum remissio sita est. Respondeo Christi mortem & passionem, quum illi per fidem unimur, ita nostram fieri, ut censeamur in eo pretium sufficiens solvisse pro peccatis omnibus quorum hactenus rei sumus, & quae per poenitentiam veram atque synceram retractavimus & deseruimus: non vero pro peccatis illis quorum adhuc rei non sumus, & ratione quorum remissione nondum indigemus, & de quibus nondum etiam potuimus agere poenitentiam, sine qua nullius peccati remissio propter Christi mortem conceditur: cum remissionem illam non aliter Christus nobis meruerit, quam sub conditione fidei & poenitentiae, per quam nobis meritum Christi applicandum est. Unde sequitur nos dici non debere absolute pretium sufficiens in Christo solvisse pro aliquo peccato, nisi per necessarios actus fidei & poenitentiae impleverimus illius respectu conditionem illam sub qua pro nobis Christus satisfecit, & remissionem illius promeruit.
pass_a_gloss: But here someone will say: Whoever converts himself to God through true faith and repentance is by that very fact united to Christ as a member to the head, and becomes one body with Christ, and so is reckoned to have suffered and died in Christ and in him to have paid a sufficient ransom for all his sins. But whoever pays a sufficient ransom remains discharged from his debt and can no longer be liable to a penalty to be undergone—in which the remission of sins consists. I answer: Christ’s death and passion, when we are united to him by faith, so become ours that we are reckoned in him to have paid a sufficient price for all the sins of which we are thus far guilty and which we have retracted and deserted through true and sincere repentance—not however for those sins of which we are not yet guilty, and on account of which we do not yet need remission, and concerning which we could not yet even have done repentance, without which remission of no sin is granted on account of Christ’s death: since Christ merited that remission for us only under the condition of faith and repentance through which Christ’s merit is to be applied to us. Whence it follows that we ought not to be said absolutely to have paid a sufficient price in Christ for any sin unless through the necessary acts of faith and repentance we have fulfilled, with respect to it, that condition under which Christ satisfied for us and merited its remission.
pass_b_english: Faith-union applies Christ’s sufficient price to sins already incurred and sincerely retracted.
Not to unincurred futures; no absolute ‘paid in Christ’ without the condition-acts for that sin.

choices.why: Applied under faith-repentance condition per sin.
rejected: covers all future sins at once
